# GrappleGraph contributor instructions

These instructions apply to the entire repository.

## Repository purpose

GrappleGraph is a Quartz 5 static study atlas for Renzo Gracie Niagara exam requirements. Preserve the distinction between academy curriculum facts and general Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu study references. Do not invent academy-specific grips, reactions, finishing positions, or verification.

## Authoritative branch and generated files

- `v5` is the production branch and the GitHub Pages deployment source.
- `upstream` is the Quartz framework remote; do not push GrappleGraph changes there.
- Never edit `public/`, `.quartz/`, `.quartz-cache/`, or `node_modules/`. They are generated.
- Keep source changes focused. Avoid wholesale Quartz framework upgrades unless the task explicitly calls for one.

## Required checks

Use Node.js 22+ and npm 10.9.2+.

Run before handing off a change:

```sh
npm run validate
```

Also run `npm run build && npm run audit:site` when content, components, styles, plugins, or assets change. Run `npm audit --omit=dev` when dependencies or the lockfile change.

`npm test` intentionally runs Quartz tests and the vendored component tests separately. Do not replace it with an unrestricted `tsx --test`, which incorrectly collects the vendored Vitest suites.

## Curriculum invariants

- Belt order is always Blue, Purple, Brown-only.
- Blue IDs are `BLU-01`–`BLU-30`.
- Purple IDs are `PUR-01`–`PUR-27`.
- Brown-only IDs are `BRO-01`–`BRO-03`.
- `exam_id` is the sequential site ID within the belt.
- `source_exam_id` is the number printed on the academy source sheet.
- Keep `instructor_verified: false` until a professor verifies the entire academy-specific sequence.
- Every technique must contain `Sequence`, `Study card`, `Key cues`, `Practice`, and `Video study` sections.
- Every technique’s sequence must directly link the concept note named by its `start`, `landing`, and `finish` metadata when that value is a position or submission.
- Every technique, position, movement, and submission note needs a direct `youtube.com/watch?v=` reference. Describe the match honestly (`full`, `parts`, `finish-only`, `representative`, and so on).
- Update `DATA_REVIEW.md` when a curriculum assumption is confirmed or a new question is identified.
- Run `npm run audit:content` after changing curriculum notes.

Use sentence case for page titles and link labels, while preserving proper technique names such as De La Riva, Americana, Kimura, Ezekiel, and X-guard.

## Links and navigation

- Prefer Quartz Wikilinks for internal content links.
- Preserve existing aliases when moving a published note.
- Use base-path-aware navigation (`resolveBasePath` or `document.body.dataset.basepath`) because production is hosted under `/grapplegraph/`.
- Use `window.spaNavigate` when available and fall back to normal browser navigation.
- The progress tracker is browser-local. Changes must preserve existing `grapplegraph-progress-v1` data and legacy-slug migration.
- Stacked pages must deduplicate canonical slugs and remain on the left side on desktop.

## Graph plugin

The customized graph source is in `vendor/grapplegraph-graph/src/`; its committed `dist/` output is generated by the package build.

When changing the graph:

1. Edit source files, not `dist/`.
2. Run `npm run check --prefix vendor/grapplegraph-graph`.
3. Run `npm run build --prefix vendor/grapplegraph-graph`.
4. Run the root validation and production build.

Keep graph filters synchronized between local and expanded views. Any asynchronous render must be cancellable or stale-safe, and every registered listener or observer must have a cleanup path across Quartz SPA navigation.

## Page-title plugin

`vendor/grapplegraph-page-title/` replaces Quartz's relative site-title link with an explicit production base path. Keep the production link at `/grapplegraph/` and the local-development link at `/`. Build and commit its `dist/` output after source changes, and preserve the generated-site audit that checks every rendered title link.

## Styling and accessibility

- Keep the Motion Atlas design system and optional dark mode.
- Reuse the existing CSS variables before introducing new colors.
- Text and interactive controls must meet WCAG AA contrast at their rendered size.
- Preserve visible keyboard focus, meaningful labels, Escape-to-close behavior, and standard keyboard interaction for tab-like controls.
- Test responsive behavior in source and generated markup. Do not fix one viewport with hard-coded coordinates that break another.

## Repository hygiene

- Use `rg` for searches.
- Keep README commands accurate when scripts or workflows change.
- Do not commit temporary design pages, screenshots, extracted PDFs, local Obsidian state, or build output.
- Retain upstream Quartz documentation unless a task explicitly requests removing it; it is useful framework reference material.
- Treat `DATA_REVIEW.md` as maintained project documentation, not scratch output.
